paper_sections.title: Effective amygdala-prefrontal connectivity predicts individual differences in successful emotion regulation
Prefrontal network underlying the down-regulation of emotion
Amygdala-prefrontal network underlying the up-regulation of emotion

description.value: The study examined whether effective connectivity between the left inferior frontal gyrus or left amygdala and other emotion-regulation regions varies with success in cognitively increasing or decreasing emotional responses to aversive pictures.

design.value: Twenty-three right-handed subjects completed an event-related fMRI emotion-reappraisal task in which they increased, decreased, or did not manipulate their emotional responses to aversive or neutral pictures. Self-reported reappraisal success was entered as an explicit predictor of task-dependent PPI connectivity.

After each emotion regulation phase subjects rated their current emotional state on a four-point Likert scale from 1 to 4, from less negative to very negative.
EDA was recorded as a physiological control measure; SCRs were defined as deflections of at least 0.01 µS occurring 1–8 s after stimulus onset.

task_description.value: Participants were presented with highly arousing and aversive pictures while using cognitive reappraisal to increase, maintain, or decrease their emotional responses. Each trial comprised a 2 s instruction cue, an 8 s picture presentation, a 4 s emotional-state rating, and a jittered 4–8 s fixation phase. One run consisted of 28 trials and each session consisted of six runs.

instructions.value: In the ‘Increase’ condition, subjects were asked to engage themselves with the depicted situation and increase their sense of subjective closeness. In the ‘Decrease’ condition, subjects were instructed to reduce the intensity of the negative emotion by distancing themselves from the image and becoming a detached observer. In the ‘Look’ conditions, subjects were asked to view the stimuli attentively and allow themselves to experience any emotional responses without trying to manipulate them.

stimuli.value: 126 aversive and 42 neutral pictures from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS). Pictures were presented centrally against a black background; the display used an 800 × 600 pixel screen subtending 32° × 24° visual angle, and pictures subtended 24° × 18°.

description.value: Functional images were acquired using a T2*-weighted, gradient-echo planar imaging pulse sequence recording 37 sections oriented parallel to the anterior and posterior commissure, with an in-plane resolution of 3 × 3 × 3 mm³, interslice gap of 0, TE = 30 ms, TR = 2 s, flip angle = 90°, field of view = 192 × 192 mm, and a 64 × 64 data acquisition matrix. For each experimental run 285 whole brain volumes were recorded.

description.value: EDA data were down-sampled offline, decomposed into continuous tonic and phasic activity, and averaged across trials within each condition using an 8 s time window. SCR amplitudes were extracted as the difference between a local minimum and the succeeding local maximum within the response window.

model_settings.value: Separate regressors were specified for the instruction cue, rating, and the four task conditions: Increase, Decrease, Look-Negative, and Look-Neutral. Look-Negative constituted the natural response control condition.

software.value: BrainVoyager QX 2.3.1, Brain Innovation, Maastricht, The Netherlands

model_settings.value: Time-series from the left amygdala and left IFG were extracted as physiological seeds by averaging neural activity within single-subject ROI masks. The Increase > Look-Negative and Decrease > Look-Negative regulation contrasts were used as psychological contexts. The PPI interaction term was entered into a voxelwise regression with the seed raw time-series and all original GLM regressors as covariates; individual reappraisal success scores were then entered as covariates to predict the PPI maps.

model_type.value: main-effect analysis of task with post-hoc t-tests

model_settings.value: Task effects were tested for emotional-state ratings and SCRs, followed by post-hoc pairwise t-tests.

description.value: Subjects viewed negative stimuli attentively and allowed themselves to experience or feel any emotional responses without trying to manipulate them. This condition represented the natural emotional response to the stimuli and was used as the control condition.

Subjects viewed neutral stimuli attentively and allowed themselves to experience any emotional responses without trying to manipulate them. This condition mainly served as a break in the task design in which no emotions were elicited.
